raw_case_text:
A 40-year-old lady presented with fever, headache, arthralgia, and myalgia, after returning from the Philippines. She recalled mosquito bite one week before. Investigations showed lymphopenia, increased hepatic enzymes, C-Reactive-Protein (CRP), normal renal function (Table 1), and prominent spleen (11.6 cm) on ultrasonogram. Empirical antibiotic was given. Septic workup was negative. Her fever subsided and hepatic enzymes were improving. Dengue-virus IgM/specific nonstructural (NS1) protein antigen, chikungunya virus (CHIKV) IgM, and blood malaria parasite were not detected. She was discharged on day 10 with stable condition.
Eight weeks later she was readmitted for fever, malaise, and persistent symmetrical polyarthritis involving both wrists, metacarpophalangeal joints, shoulders, hips, and knees, mimicking RA. She reported no recent hiking, no rash, and no oral ulcer. Clinical examination revealed more than ten tender and swollen joints over hands, wrists, and knees. There was no lymphadenopathy and no focal neurological deficit. Blood tests showed elevated liver enzymes, ferritin, and persistent high CRP level (Table 1). Hepatitis A, B, and C serology, anti-HIV, autoantibodies including rheumatoid factor, anticyclic-citrullinated peptide, anti-nuclear antibody, antidouble-stranded-DNA, anti-neutrophil-cytoplasmic antibody, anti-smooth-muscle antibody, and anti-mitochondrial antibody were all negative. C3 and C4 levels were normal. There was no erosion on hands and knees radiographs and her chest X-ray was clear. She was covered with Augmentin and Doxycycline for fever. No vegetation was detected on echocardiogram. Hepatic ultrasonogram showed prominent periportal echogenicity. Musculoskeletal ultrasound demonstrated wrists extensors and flexors tenosynovitis with increased Doppler signals, effusion, and synovial proliferation in knees (Figure 1). A total 25 mL fluid was aspirated from left knee suprapatellar recess. Gram stain, bacterial culture, and acid-fast-bacilli smear were negative. Fever persisted for two weeks. Liver biopsy was suggested to look for infective or infiltrative causes but patient refused. Septic workup was all unrevealing. CHIKV serology was rechecked. This time CHIKV-IgM was detected and CHIKV-polyvalent-antibody titre had risen from 1 : <10 to 1 : 1280. The first CHIKV-IgM negative sample was reexamined and was CHIKV-PCR positive (Table 1). The diagnosis of CHIKV-related arthritis was made. She was treated with supportive measures. Liver enzymes slowly reduced but joint symptoms persisted. Patient requested discharge-against-medical-advice after 3 weeks of hospital stay.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 40-year-old woman presented with fever, malaise, and persistent symmetrical polyarthritis affecting the wrists, hands, shoulders, hips, and knees 8 weeks after an acute post-travel febrile illness.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Eight weeks prior to readmission, the patient returned from the Philippines (recalling a mosquito bite 1 week earlier) and presented with acute fever, headache, arthralgia, and myalgia. Initial workup showed lymphopenia, elevated liver enzymes, elevated CRP, normal renal function, splenomegaly (11.6 cm on ultrasound), and negative dengue IgM/NS1, chikungunya IgM, malaria smear, and septic workup; she received empiric antibiotics and was discharged stable on day 10. Eight weeks later, she was readmitted with recurrent fever, malaise, and persistent symmetrical polyarthritis involving bilateral wrists, MCP joints, shoulders, hips, and knees mimicking rheumatoid arthritis.
subjective.past_medical_history: Travel to the Philippines with mosquito bite 1 week prior to initial febrile episode.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, malaise, and symmetrical polyarthritis; negative for recent hiking, skin rash, or oral ulcers.

objective.physical_examination: More than 10 tender and swollen joints involving the hands, wrists, and knees. No lymphadenopathy and no focal neurological deficits.
objective.routine_investigations: Blood tests: elevated liver enzymes, elevated serum ferritin, and persistently high CRP; normal C3 and C4 complement levels. Viral hepatitis serology (hepatitis A, B, and C) and anti-HIV: negative. Hand and knee radiographs: no bone erosions. Chest X-ray: clear. Echocardiogram: no vegetations. Abdominal ultrasound: prominent periportal hepatic echogenicity (initial admission showed 11.6 cm splenomegaly). Musculoskeletal ultrasound: wrist extensor and flexor tenosynovitis with increased power Doppler signals, knee joint effusion, and synovial proliferation.
objective.advanced_workup: Autoimmune panel: rheumatoid factor (RF), anti-CCP, ANA, anti-dsDNA, ANCA, anti-smooth muscle antibody (ASMA), and anti-mitochondrial antibody (AMA) all negative. Left knee arthrocentesis (25 mL aspirated from suprapatellar recess): negative Gram stain, bacterial culture, and acid-fast bacilli (AFB) smear. Liver biopsy was recommended to evaluate persistent fever and hepatic abnormalities, but the patient declined.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Chikungunya virus-related chronic symmetrical polyarthritis and hepatitis. Septic arthritis, infective endocarditis, viral hepatitis, malaria, dengue, and autoimmune rheumatic diseases (RA, SLE) were excluded. Confirmation: Repeat serology on readmission was positive for CHIKV-IgM with a rise in CHIKV polyvalent antibody titer from <1:10 to 1:1,280, and retrospective testing of the first admission's IgM-negative serum sample was positive for CHIKV by RT-PCR. Management and outcome: Treated initially with empiric amoxicillin-clavulanate (Augmentin) and doxycycline during the 2-week persistent fever, followed by supportive measures. Liver enzymes gradually improved, though joint symptoms persisted, and the patient took discharge against medical advice after a 3-week hospitalization.
